title: Interpreting Patient-Reported Outcomes — Floor and Ceiling Effects, MCID by Anchor or Distribution

hook.en: A patient scores 85 out of 100 on a function questionnaire at the start, and 90 at the end. Success? Perhaps not: the questionnaire may have run out of room to show improvement. Learn how to read patient-reported scores with care.
hook.ur: Mareez function questionnaire par shuru mein 100 mein se 85 aur aakhir mein 90 score karta hai. Kamyabi? Shayad nahi: ho sakta hai questionnaire mein behtari dikhane ki jagah khatam ho gayi ho. Patient-reported scores ko ehtiyat se parhna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain floor and ceiling effects, tell an anchor-based MCID from a distribution-based one, judge individual change against group change, and choose a patient-reported measure that fits your patients.
goal.ur: End tak aap floor aur ceiling effects samjhayenge, anchor-based MCID ko distribution-based se alag karenge, infiradi tabdeeli ka group ki tabdeeli se muqabla karenge, aur apne mareezon ke liye munasib patient-reported measure chunenge.

text.en: A **patient-reported outcome measure (PROM)** is a questionnaire answered by the patient about symptoms, function or quality of life. A **floor effect** means many patients score at the lowest possible value, so deterioration cannot be seen; a **ceiling effect** means many score at the highest, so improvement cannot be seen. A common rule is that more than 15 percent at the extreme is a concern. The **MCID** (minimal clinically important difference) can be estimated by **anchor-based** methods (linking the change in score to the patient's own rating of "a little better") or **distribution-based** methods (using statistics such as a fraction of the standard deviation). Anchor-based is closer to patient meaning.
text.ur: **Patient-reported outcome measure (PROM)** ek questionnaire hai jis ka jawab mareez alamaat, function ya zindagi ki quality ke baare mein deta hai. **Floor effect** ka matlab hai ke bohat se mareez sab se kam mumkina value par score karte hain, isliye girawat nazar nahi aati; **ceiling effect** ka matlab hai bohat se sab se zyada par score karte hain, isliye behtari nazar nahi aati. Aam qaida hai ke intehai par 15 fisad se zyada fikr ki baat hai. **MCID** (minimal clinically important difference) ka andaaza **anchor-based** tareeqon (score ki tabdeeli ko mareez ki apni "thora behtar" ki rating se jorna) ya **distribution-based** tareeqon (standard deviation ke hisse jaisi shumariyat) se lagaya ja sakta hai. Anchor-based mareez ke maani ke qareeb hai.

text.en: Think of **a ruler that only goes from 10 to 90 centimetres**. A child shorter than 10 or an adult taller than 90 cannot be measured. A questionnaire with floor or ceiling effects is that ruler. Nothing is wrong with the person; the tool simply runs out.
text.ur: **Aisa farsh jo sirf 10 se 90 centimetre tak hai** sochein. 10 se chhota bacha ya 90 se lamba baalig naapa nahi ja sakta. Floor ya ceiling effect wala questionnaire woh farsh hai. Insaan mein koi kharabi nahi; aala bas khatam ho jata hai.

rows.en: Compares score change with a patient's global rating of change, such as "a little better"
rows.ur: Score ki tabdeeli ko mareez ki kul tabdeeli ki rating se milata hai, jaise "thora behtar"

rows.en: Reflects patient meaning, but depends on the anchor chosen and may be affected by recall
rows.ur: Mareez ke maani ko zahir karta hai, lekin chune gaye anchor par munhasir aur yaadasht se mutasir ho sakta hai

rows.en: Uses statistics, for example half a standard deviation or the standard error of measurement
rows.ur: Shumariyat istemal karta hai, masalan aadha standard deviation ya naap ki standard error

rows.en: Easy to compute, but does not tell you what patients feel is important
rows.ur: Hisab aasaan, lekin yeh nahi batata ke mareez kya ahem samajhte hain

rows.en: Prefer anchor-based, supported by distribution values, and in a population like yours
rows.ur: Anchor-based ko tarjeeh dein, distribution values ki himayat ke saath, aur aap jaisi aabadi mein

rows.en: MCID differs by condition, severity and population
rows.ur: MCID halat, shiddat aur aabadi ke hisaab se mukhtalif hota hai

question.en: A questionnaire has a maximum score of 100. At the start of a study, 40 percent of patients already score above 95. What is the problem?
question.ur: Questionnaire ka zyada se zyada score 100 hai. Study ke aaghaz mein 40 fisad mareez pehle se 95 se oopar score karte hain. Masla kya hai?

text.en: A ceiling effect: improvement cannot be shown in these patients, so the questionnaire is not suitable
text.ur: Ceiling effect: in mareezon mein behtari dikhayi nahi ja sakti, isliye questionnaire munasib nahi

feedback.en: Yes — more than 15 percent at the ceiling limits what it can detect.
feedback.ur: Haan — ceiling par 15 fisad se zyada isko dhoondhne ki salahiyat mehdood karta hai.

feedback.en: Scores are high, so it is the ceiling.
feedback.ur: Scores zyada hain, isliye ceiling hai.

text.en: There is no problem; high scores mean good care
text.ur: Koi masla nahi; zyada scores ka matlab achhi care

feedback.en: It indicates limited room to detect change.
feedback.ur: Yeh tabdeeli dhoondhne ki kam gunjaish dikhata hai.

question.en: The published MCID of a questionnaire is 10 points, based on young athletes with knee injuries. Your patients are frail 80-year-olds with arthritis. What is the best approach?
question.ur: Questionnaire ka shaya shuda MCID 10 point hai, jo ghutne ki chot wale jawan athletes par mabni hai. Aap ke mareez kamzor 80 saal ke arthritis wale hain. Behtareen tareeqa kya hai?

feedback.en: It may not fit a different population.
feedback.ur: Yeh mukhtalif aabadi ke liye fit na ho.

text.en: Use it with caution; look for an MCID from a population like yours, and discuss meaningful change with the patient
text.ur: Ehtiyat se istemal karein; aap jaisi aabadi se MCID dhoondhein, aur ba-maani tabdeeli par mareez se baat karein

question.en: A group of patients improves by an average of 12 points, which exceeds the MCID of 10. Does this mean every patient improved meaningfully?
question.ur: Mareezon ka ek group average mein 12 point behtar hota hai, jo 10 ke MCID se zyada hai. Kya iska matlab har mareez ne ba-maani behtari ki?

feedback.en: That compares the average, not each person.
feedback.ur: Yeh average ka muqabla hai, har shakhs ka nahi.

text.en: No; the average can hide individuals who improved little and others who improved a lot; look at the proportion of patients who exceeded the MCID
text.ur: Nahi; average aise afraad ko chhupa sakta hai jinhon ne kam behtari ki aur doosre jinhon ne zyada; un mareezon ka hissa dekhein jinhon ne MCID se zyada kiya

feedback.en: Yes — responder analysis shows the spread.
feedback.ur: Haan — responder analysis phailao dikhata hai.

text.en: **Using one MCID for everything.** MCIDs vary by condition, severity, time and the method used. Another trap is to compare an individual patient's change with a group MCID without considering measurement error (MDC). Also, do not use PROMs only for research: discuss scores with patients, since the numbers are less important than the story they open.
text.ur: **Har cheez ke liye ek MCID.** MCID halat, shiddat, waqt aur istemal shuda tareeqe ke hisaab se mukhtalif hote hain. Ek aur jaal ek mareez ki tabdeeli ko naap ki ghalti (MDC) par ghaur kiye baghair group MCID se milana hai. PROMs ko sirf research ke liye istemal na karein: scores par mareezon se baat karein, kyunke numbers us kahani se kam ahem hain jo woh kholte hain.

text.en: **Use PROMs as a conversation.** At the first visit, choose a short PROM and one patient-chosen goal. At follow-up, look at the change together: "You went from 40 to 55. What can you do now that you could not before?" This turns a number into meaning and keeps care on what matters to the patient.
text.ur: **PROMs ko baat cheet ke taur par istemal karein.** Pehli visit par chhota PROM aur mareez ka chuna hua ek maqsad chunein. Follow-up par tabdeeli milkar dekhein: "Aap 40 se 55 par aaye. Ab aap kya kar sakte hain jo pehle nahi kar sakte the?" Isse number maani mein badalta hai aur care mareez ke liye ahem cheez par rehti hai.

question.en: Why can the same change score mean different things at different starting points?
question.ur: Wohi tabdeeli ka score mukhtalif aaghaz ke points par mukhtalif matlab kyun rakhta hai?

answer.en: Patients who start with very poor scores often have more room to improve, and regression to the mean pushes extreme scores towards the middle on repeat. Patients who start near the ceiling have little room. Also, the same number of points may feel different at different levels of function. This is why baseline score should be considered when interpreting change.
answer.ur: Jo mareez bohat kharab scores se shuru karte hain unhein aksar behtar hone ki zyada jagah hoti hai, aur regression to the mean dohrane par intehai scores ko darmiyan ki taraf dhakelta hai. Jo mareez ceiling ke qareeb se shuru karte hain unhein kam jagah hoti hai. Saath hi wahi points ki ginti function ki mukhtalif satahon par mukhtalif mehsoos ho sakti hai. Isi liye tabdeeli ki tafseer mein baseline score par ghaur karna chahiye.

beats.patient: A therapist uses a 0-to-100 hand function questionnaire. A patient with a wrist fracture scores 30 at the start and 52 at 8 weeks. The published anchor-based MCID is 12 points in a similar group.
beats.assessment: The change of 22 points exceeds the MCID and probably the MDC, so it is both real and meaningful.
beats.treatment: She discusses with the patient which activities have returned (dressing, cooking) and which have not (lifting a kettle), and sets the next goals.
beats.reassess: The numbers and the patient's own account agree, and the plan is shaped by what matters to him.

text.en: **A good score does not mean it is safe to progress.** A high PROM score does not replace a physical examination or red-flag screening. Likewise, a worsening score may signal a new problem, such as infection or complex pain, that deserves assessment, not just more of the same treatment.
text.ur: **Achha score ka matlab yeh nahi ke aage barhna mehfooz hai.** Zyada PROM score jismani muaine ya red-flag screening ki jagah nahi leta. Isi tarah girta hua score koi naya masla, jaise infection ya pechida dard, ka ishara de sakta hai jis ka assessment chahiye, sirf wahi ilaaj mazeed nahi.

text.en: Terwee and colleagues proposed quality criteria for measurement properties of health-status questionnaires, including that floor or ceiling effects are present when more than 15 percent of respondents achieve the lowest or highest possible score. Revicki and colleagues recommended that minimally important differences for patient-reported outcomes be determined primarily with anchor-based methods, supported by distribution-based methods, and that results be interpreted in the context of the population and design.
text.ur: Terwee aur saathiyon ne health-status questionnaires ki naap ki khasiyaton ke quality criteria tajweez kiye, jin mein yeh ke floor ya ceiling effect tab hota hai jab 15 fisad se zyada jawab dene wale sab se kam ya sab se zyada mumkina score hasil karein. Revicki aur saathiyon ne sifarish ki ke patient-reported outcomes ke liye minimally important differences zyada tar anchor-based tareeqon se tay hon, distribution-based tareeqon ki himayat ke saath, aur nateeje aabadi aur design ke context mein parhe jayen.

text.en: **Room, Anchor, Individual, Talk.** Check room to improve (floor and ceiling), prefer anchor-based MCIDs, look at individuals and talk about the score.
text.ur: **Gunjaish, Anchor, Infiradi, Baat.** Behtar hone ki gunjaish (floor aur ceiling) dekhein, anchor-based MCIDs ko tarjeeh dein, afraad ko dekhein aur score par baat karein.

summary.en: Floor and ceiling effects (more than about 15 percent at an extreme) limit a questionnaire's ability to show change.
summary.ur: Floor aur ceiling effects (intehai par takreeban 15 fisad se zyada) questionnaire ki tabdeeli dikhane ki salahiyat mehdood karte hain.

summary.en: Anchor-based MCIDs reflect patient meaning; distribution-based ones are statistical and best used as support.
summary.ur: Anchor-based MCIDs mareez ke maani ko zahir karte hain; distribution-based shumariyati hain aur madad ke taur par behtar.

summary.en: Interpret change for individuals, not only group averages, and use PROMs as a conversation.
summary.ur: Tabdeeli ko sirf group averages nahi balke afraad ke liye parhein, aur PROMs ko baat cheet ke taur par istemal karein.

back.en: Many patients score at the maximum, so improvement cannot be detected.
back.ur: Bohat se mareez zyada se zyada score karte hain, isliye behtari dhoondhi nahi ja sakti.

front.ur: Anchor-based MCID kya istemal karta hai?

back.en: The patient's own rating of change as a reference.
back.ur: Mareez ki apni tabdeeli ki rating bataur hawala.

front.en: Is the MCID the same for all populations?
front.ur: Kya MCID har aabadi ke liye ek jaisa hai?

back.en: No; it varies by condition, severity and method.
back.ur: Nahi; yeh halat, shiddat aur tareeqe se mukhtalif hai.

front.en: Why look at individuals as well as the average?
front.ur: Average ke saath afraad ko bhi kyun dekhein?

back.en: Averages can hide people who improved little or a lot.
back.ur: Averages un logon ko chhupa sakte hain jinhon ne kam ya zyada behtari ki.
